Dia de los Angelitos

Dia de los Angelitos: Honoring Little Spirits

Celebrate the first day of Día de los Muertos by welcoming the angelitos, the souls of departed children, with heartfelt traditions and special treats.

  1. Morning

    Prepare the altar

    Begin the day by setting up a vibrant altar with candles, paper cut-outs, toys, and marigold flowers to warmly welcome the angelitos home.

  2. Late Morning

    Bake Pan de Muerto

    Bake tiny loaves of Pan de Muerto, a traditional sweet bread symbolizing the cycle of life and death, to place as offerings on the altar.

    Recipes: Pan de Muerto

  3. Noon

    Make Atole

    Prepare warm atole, a comforting corn-based drink, to share with family and offer to the angelitos as part of the feast.

    Recipes: Traditional Atole

  4. Afternoon

    Decorate sugar skulls

    Decorate sugar skulls with bright colors and patterns, representing the joyful spirits of the children and adding them to the altar.

    Recipes: Traditional Sugar Skulls

  5. Late Afternoon

    Scatter marigolds and ring bells

    Walk around your home scattering marigold petals and ringing bells to guide the angelitos to their altar and invite their presence.

  6. Evening

    Family gathering and feast

    Gather with loved ones to enjoy the offerings, share stories, and remember the children with love and warmth.

    Recipes: Traditional Atole · Traditional Sugar Skulls · Pan de Muerto

End the day with a quiet moment at the glowing altar, feeling connected to the angelitos and the cherished memories they bring.
